newsitem.title: USA: Kellogg's profits plunge 30 percent in ongoing price war.
newsitem.headline: Kellogg's profits plunge 30 percent in ongoing price war.

text.p: Kellogg Co. said Friday that its profits plunged more than 30 percent in the third quarter as a continuing price war in the U.S. breakfast cereal market reduced its overall sales.

The company, the world's biggest maker of ready-to-eat breakfast cereals, said its net income for the three months ended Sept. 30 fell to $159.1 million, or 75 cents a share, from $230.0 million, or $1.05 a share.
Kellogg said its overall sales slipped 9 percent to $1.68 billion from $1.84 billion as continued weak prices for breakfast cereals offset a 1 percent gain in wordlwide sales volume.

The maker of Kellogg's Corn Flakes, Frosted Flakes, Rice Krispies, Fruit Loops and Special-K reduced prices on about two-thirds of its breakfast cereals in June as it battled General Mills Inc., Post and Quaker Oats Co. for a bigger share of the huge American breakfast cereal market.

The company said that excluding certain one-time charges of $24.8 million, or 10 cents a share, its net income would have been $180.3 million, or 85 cents a share -- right in line with a company projection on Sept. 4 and Wall Street expectations according to First Call, which tracks analysts' estimates.
Kellogg's stock added 75 cents to $66.25 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.

"As previously forecast, our third-quarter performance was influenced significantly by competitive conditions in the U.S. cereal category," Chairman Arnold G. Langbo said in a statement. "We continue to believe our strategy of lower prices combined with efficient promotion spending is the right strategy to deliver long-term growth."

Kellogg, based in Battle Creek, Mich., said its global sales volume increased 1 percent to a record level, with strength in convenience foods and cereals outside the United States more than offsetting continued softness in U.S. cereal volume.

The company, which also makes a variety of convenience and snack foods, said the third-quarter charges included a $15 million provision for the potential settlement of litigation, with the rest related to ongoing productivity and operational streamlining initiatives.

For the first nine months, Kellogg said its net income declined to $443.7 million, or $2.08 a share, from $561.9 million, or $2.56 a share. Excluding one-time charges, the company said, net income would have been $488 million, or $2.29 a share.
Nine-months sales dipped to $5.12 billion from $5.34 billion.
